headline: Attackers exploit an unpatched Fastjson RCE and chain fresh PTC product-lifecycle flaws for Cl0p extortion, while cybercrime tooling from SourTrade malvertising to DevMan's ransomware portal grows steadily more industrialized.

emerging_trends.text: Cybercriminals keep industrializing their operations, from DevMan's self-service ransomware portal that hands affiliates payload builders and payout dashboards to SourTrade's malvertising that turns victims' own browsers into malware compilers.
emerging_trends.topic_title: DevMan RaaS Portal Centralizes Affiliate Operations

emerging_trends.text: Attackers are racing to weaponize enterprise-software flaws, exploiting the unpatched Fastjson library inside Spring Boot applications and chaining fresh PTC Windchill and FlexPLM bugs to feed Cl0p's data-extortion campaign.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Unpatched Fastjson RCE CVE-2026-16723 Under Attack

emerging_trends.text: Phishing crews are compressing the kill chain, with insurance-focused operations now hijacking accounts in real time as victims type their credentials rather than banking them for later use.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Insurance Phishing Shifts to Real-Time Account Hijacking

topics.title: SourTrade Malvertising Builds Malware in the Browser
topics.latest_developments: Confiant named the campaign SourTrade on July 23 and traced it to late 2024, finding it uses the legitimate Bun runtime as its base while victims' browsers assemble the final Windows executable in memory from pieces instead of downloading one complete file.
topics.summary: SourTrade serves counterfeit TradingView, Solana, and Luno pages to retail cryptocurrency traders, and malicious JavaScript directs the browser to compile the malware itself, evading URL-based detection. Traders should reach these platforms through bookmarks and treat sponsored search results with suspicion.

sources.title: Malvertising Sends Malware in Pieces, Then Makes the Browser Build the Executable
Malicious sites use JavaScript to build malware in browser memory

topics.title: Unpatched Fastjson RCE CVE-2026-16723 Under Attack
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News detailed on July 25 that the confirmed chain hits affected Spring Boot applications, where a single malicious JSON request runs code unauthenticated at the Java process's privileges, and that Alibaba rates the flaw 9.0 while shipping no fix.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-16723 sits in Fastjson 1.x, Alibaba's widely used JSON library for Java. Attackers who reach a vulnerable endpoint run code without authentication; with no patch available, defenders must restrict exposure and filter untrusted JSON input.

sources.title: Fastjson 1.x RCE Vulnerability Targeted in Attacks With No Patched Available

topics.title: Rockwell Patches Arena Simulation Code-Execution Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Rockwell Automation patched code-execution vulnerabilities in its Arena simulation software on July 25 after a researcher showed how an attacker could exploit them against industrial organizations.
topics.summary: The flaws let an attacker run code on machines running Arena, Rockwell's discrete-event simulation tool used across industrial engineering. Operators should apply the fixes and keep engineering workstations off untrusted networks.

sources.title: Rockwell Patches Code Execution Flaws in Arena Simulation Software

topics.title: Clop Extortion Campaign Hits PTC Windchill and FlexPLM
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News laid out the exploit chain on July 25: Cl0p affiliates pair a pre-authentication information-disclosure flaw in the FlexPLM WSDL endpoint with a server-side bug in the Windchill login servlet to run code without authentication.
topics.summary: Cl0p, also tracked as Chubby Scorpius, FIN11, Graceful Spider, and Lace Tempest, is stealing data from internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM product-lifecycle-management servers for extortion. Organizations running these systems should pull them off the public internet and hunt for the chain.

sources.title: Cl0p Affiliates Target Internet-Exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM with Unauthenticated RCE

topics.title: DevMan RaaS Portal Centralizes Affiliate Operations
topics.latest_developments: Swiss firm PRODAFT disclosed on July 25 that the DevMan ransomware-as-a-service operation, which it tracks as Funky Mantis, runs a dedicated web portal that lets affiliates build payloads, manage victims, and track earnings from a single console.
topics.summary: DevMan's centrally administered platform bundles payload generation, finances, and victim management into one interface, lowering the skill floor for affiliates. Defenders should watch for payloads bearing its build signatures.

sources.title: DevMan RaaS Portal Centralizes Payload Builds, Victim Management, and Affiliate Payouts

topics.title: Insurance Phishing Shifts to Real-Time Account Hijacking
topics.latest_developments: CTM360 reported on July 25 that insurance-focused phishing has dropped the old harvest-now, exploit-later model and now hijacks accounts in real time, capturing credentials and taking over accounts as victims enter them.
topics.summary: The insurance-sector campaigns seize accounts the moment a victim submits credentials, defeating defenses timed to catch later logins. Institutions should enforce phishing-resistant authentication and monitor for live session hijacking.

sources.title: CTM360 Research Reveals How Insurance Phishing Has Evolved Into Real-Time Account Hijacking

business.title: Arnold Palmer Airport Shutdown Reshuffles Regional Air Travel
business.latest_developments: The shutdown of Arnold Palmer Regional Airport in Unity Township is sending Westmoreland County travelers to other runways and opening a window for competing regional airfields, TribLive reported.
business.summary: With Arnold Palmer Regional Airport in Unity Township closed, fliers such as Michelle Kish now route trips through Atlanta and other regional airports rather than Pittsburgh International, creating a sudden opening for nearby runways to pick up traffic.

business.title: Little Debbie Driver Charged in $17,000 Fraud
business.latest_developments: The City of Washington Police Department charged a Little Debbie delivery driver with running a $17,000 scheme, selling snacks for cash at flea markets while filing fake invoices to make it look like stores had bought the product.
business.summary: James Powell, 39, of Valley Grove, West Virginia, sold his Little Debbie route inventory for cash at flea markets across Washington County and submitted thousands of dollars of bogus invoices to cover the sales, police said; the City of Washington police opened the case in May after the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office flagged it.

sources.title: Little Debbie snack delivery driver charged in $17,000 fraud scheme

around_town.title: State Police Traffic Stops Show No Racial Disparities
around_town.latest_developments: An analysis released Friday found no substantive racial or ethnic disparities in Pennsylvania State Police traffic stops for a third straight year, officials said.
around_town.summary: The Pennsylvania State Police's third annual independent review of trooper traffic-stop data found no substantive racial or ethnic disparities in who officers pull over, officials announced Friday.
